title: The vaccine that crossed the ocean arm to arm

scenes.text: 1803. Refrigerators don't exist. How do you carry a vaccine across the ocean without it spoiling?
The Balmis expedition's answer: inside an arm. Twenty-two boys from the foundling home in Corunna form a living chain.
One child is vaccinated. Days later, the vaccine passes from his arm to the next. And so on, arm to arm, for the whole voyage.
They are cared for by Isabel Zendal, head of the foundling home.
The Canaries, Puerto Rico, Venezuela, Cuba, Mexico, the Philippines… all the way to China. In Venezuela alone, more than twelve thousand people vaccinated in under a month.
And when they left, they set up vaccination boards to carry on. Medical historians call it the first international vaccination campaign in history.
Share it with someone who thinks logistics is boring.
